# Extract — Treasury payment calendar, FY2026 (rev. 2026-05)

Provided by: Treasury Analyst (Renata Kowalczyk), 2026-06-12
Source document: "AP & Treasury Payment Calendar FY2026", Finance shared
drive, tab `Calendar` and tab `Cutoffs`. Extract covers the two tabs in
full; the third tab (`Bank contacts`) was not provided.

## Standing weekly cycle

| Day | Step | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tuesday 16:00 | Invoice batch cut for the week's proposal | AP Clerk |
| Wednesday 12:00 | Proposal assembled in NetSuite, cash position attached | AP Manager |
| Thursday 15:00 | Proposal sent to Controller for approval | AP Manager |
| Friday 09:30 | NACHA file built and uploaded (Chase Connect) | Treasury Analyst |
| Friday 11:00 | Release | Corporate Controller |
| Monday 10:00 | Bank statement pull for the prior week | Treasury Analyst |

Note on the calendar itself, cell `Calendar!B14`: "Wire requests outside
the Friday run are by exception only — Controller approval by mail, no
proposal." No approval threshold is stated for off-cycle wires anywhere in
the calendar.

## Cutoffs and exceptions

- Month-end: the Friday run moves to the last business day, and the
  Tuesday batch cut moves forward one day. Four dates in FY2026 are
  flagged where month-end and the standing Friday collide; the calendar
  says "run once, do not double."
- Quarter-end (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec): a second run is scheduled Wednesday of
  the final week "for anything the auditors will look at."
- Bank holidays: eight dates listed. Each carries a shifted upload day; no
  shifted release day is listed, and three of the eight leave upload and
  release on the same recorded day with no separation noted.

## Statement reconciliation

Tab `Cutoffs`, block 3: statement reconciliation is scheduled monthly, "by
the 10th," owner recorded as *Treasury Analyst / AP Manager* — both names
in one cell, no split of duties. Worksheet location is given as
`Finance/Treasury/Recs/FY2026/` with the note "carry forward prior month's
unexplained items." Nothing in the calendar states who reviews a completed
worksheet, or what happens to an item that carries forward twice.

## Cash position

The cash position sheet feeding the Wednesday proposal is described as
"treasury's own workbook, refreshed Wednesday morning from the two
operating accounts." The calendar does not record where that workbook
lives or who else may edit it.
